title: Glossary
lead: Every term in the palace, defined and linked.
summary: One alphabetized reference for the whole MemPalace vocabulary: the spatial model (wings, rooms, drawers, closets, hallways, tunnels, diary), the retrieval stack (hybrid BM25 + vector, HNSW, cosine distance, the L0-L3 wake-up layers), the ingestion machinery (AAAK dialect, incremental ingest, sweeps, entity disambiguation, corpus origin), and the cross-cutting principles (local-first, BYOK, privacy by architecture). Each of the 100+ definitions ends with a pointer to the page that covers it in depth.

searchDoc.summary: An alphabetized reference for the entire MemPalace vocabulary, with each of the 100+ terms ending in a pointer to the page that covers it in depth. Covers the spatial model, the retrieval stack, the ingestion machinery, and the cross-cutting design principles.
searchDoc.body: The Glossary is a single alphabetized reference covering more than one hundred MemPalace terms, each ending with a pointer to the page that explains it fully. It draws every distinct domain term from the per-page concept sidecars and merges duplicate definitions, keeping the clearest one. The spatial-model vocabulary is the backbone: a wing is a broad person or project category, a room is a time or topic grouping inside it, and a drawer is an immutable ~800-char chunk of verbatim source text identified by a deterministic SHA-256 ID. Closets are the compact index records that hold topic, entity, and quote pointer lines back to drawers, packed greedily to 1500 chars. Hallways connect entity pairs within a wing, tunnels link rooms across wings, and a diary is a dated transcript whose content_date enables temporal grouping. A living Dynamics layer (Hebbian strength, Ebbinghaus decay, Cepeda spacing) ranks those connections by real use. The retrieval stack defines hybrid search as a two-stage process: semantic top-50 candidates from the HNSW vector index, then a convex re-score of 0.6 times vector similarity plus 0.4 times normalized Okapi-BM25, with closet boost and temporal proximity. Cosine distance lives in the [0,2] range, effective distance is the value after boost, and BM25-only over SQLite FTS5 is the graceful fallback when the vector index is corrupt. The L0-L3 wake-up stack injects context on demand: L0 identity, L1 essential story (~600-900 tokens together), L2 wing/room retrieval, and L3 deep semantic search. Ingestion terms cover the AAAK dialect (a pipe-separated symbolic index an LLM scans in one pass), idempotent and incremental ingest, drawer sweeps, NORMALIZE_VERSION, the COCA content-word filter, the two-signal-category rule, corpus-origin detection, and virtual line numbering. The knowledge-graph terms include RDF-style triples, validity windows, as_of temporal queries, invalidation, provenance fields, and timelines. Cross-cutting principles are defined too: local-first execution, BYOK external providers that are never silent, privacy by architecture, never-silent-fallback, input-validation sanitizers, symlink defense, and MCP stdio protection. Storage abstractions such as BaseBackend, BaseCollection, PalaceRef, and the typed QueryResult and GetResult dataclasses round out the list, along with i18n concepts like BCP 47 tags, combining marks, script-aware boundaries, and Matryoshka representation learning. Each entry links to architecture, palace-model, search, entities, knowledge-graph, backends, hooks, and the other detailed pages.
